title: Spectral Perturbation Bounds for Low-Rank Approximation with Applications

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper uses the Sherman–Morrison–Woodbury formula to obtain (zI − A)^{-1} − (zI − 	ilde{A})^{-1} = (zI − A)^{-1} E (zI − 	ilde{A})^{-1}. The correct identity is (zI−	ilde{A})^{-1}−(zI−A)^{-1} = (zI−	ilde{A})^{-1} E (zI−A)^{-1} (or with a sign flip). The stated identity has the wrong order of resolvent factors and a sign error, which invalidates the subsequent bootstrapping derivation that separates F(f) into F1(f) plus a term involving F(f). The whole proof of Lemma 3.1 and the main results that depend on it is therefore incorrect.
Lemma 3.1 states the condition δ_p > 5‖E‖, but Theorem 2.1 assumes 4‖E‖ < δ_p. The proof of Lemma 3.1 later uses 4‖E‖, indicating an inconsistency in the stated hypotheses.

The theorem claims a bound of O(‖E‖ λ_p/δ_p), but the actual proof in Appendix D.1 yields a term with a logarithmic factor, e.g., ~ 6‖E‖(log(6σ_1/δ_p) + λ_p/δ_p). The stated O(·) bound suppresses a log factor that is not generally absorbable, so the theorem as written is unsubstantiated.

The theorem uses ∂Γ₁ to denote the boundary of a rectangle, but earlier Γ₁ was defined as a single vertical segment of the contour (e.g., Section 3, Γ₁ = {(x₀, t) | -T ≤ t ≤ T}). This inconsistent notation makes the statement ambiguous.

The paper describes a 'novel spectral regularization preprocessing (which adds 0.1·λ₁·I to the covariance matrix)' and claims this ensures the gap condition 4‖E‖<δ_p holds. However, adding a multiple of the identity shifts all eigenvalues equally, so the eigengap δ_p = λ_p−λ_{p+1} remains unchanged. This preprocessing cannot affect whether the gap condition is satisfied, so the claim is false.
In the setting paragraph the Adult dataset is given as n=14 ("Adult dataset (n=14)"), but later the gap-check sentence says "For Adult (n=6, p=4)". The dimension changes without explanation.

The text says "we include a synthetic high-dimensional matrix (n=1200) with exponentially decaying spectrum to stress-test our bounds", but no results for this matrix appear in the figures or discussion; only Census, KDD, and Adult are shown.
Reference [47] (a recent survey) is cited but is not present in the reference list. The list ends at [46].
References [48], [49], [50] are cited in connection with the bootstrapping argument but are not included in the reference list.

Reference [41] (Van Huffel & Vandewalle, 1989) is cited for the spectral norm of random matrices (‖E‖=(2+o(1))√n). The actual paper concerns total least squares and does not provide such a result. The proper citation for this fact is the other cited work [43] (Vu, 2007) or similar.

The corollary states the condition δ_p ≥ 8.01√n as a precise constant. This figure is not rigorously justified; the actual threshold depends on the (asymptotic) constant in the bound on ‖E‖ for Wigner matrices and should be stated as 'there exists a constant c such that if δ_p ≥ c√n…'.
